name: Hakushika
about: Tatsuuma Honke Brewing makes Hakushika in Nishinomiya, in the Nada sake region of Hyogo. By the company's account, the first head, Kichizaemon, dug a well on his grounds in 1662 and began brewing with its clear water, making sake casks as a sideline. The name comes from a Chinese tale of a white deer that lived a thousand years.

Later the family sold water from the same well to other Nada brewers, who called it Miyamizu. In 1920 a Tamba tōji brewed the first Kuromatsu Hakushika. The war destroyed 35 of its 53 storehouses, and the 1995 earthquake wrecked its historic brick brewery.
